content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors of the paper propose to instill CP organization of biological NNs into the self-attention mechanism to come up with a new transformer architecture, CPViT. To do this, authors adopt previously proposed CP generation and detection algorithms. Then, a novel CP graph-guided self-attention mechanism is introduced. To distribute patches to either core or periphery nodes, authors make use of gradient flow. An extensive search on (# of Core nodes, # of nodes) space is performed to figure out the optimal (CR, Top1accuracy) pair. The authors demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach against ViT and DeiT baselines, as well as other CPViT variants. Promising results are obtained on medial and natural image classification in terms of efficiency and performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
- Core patch visualization analysis is really cool and increases the explainability of the technique.
- Novel approach to improve performance and efficiency of the vanilla ViT.
- Nice to see the decrease in CR as well as the increase in Top1accuracy.

Weaknesses
- Page 1 Introduction missing spacing.
- 3.2 "16 × 16 = 196" I understand that images are of size 224x224, and designating 16x16 patches amount to 14^2=196 patches. However, denoting it like this is pretty ambiguous.
- A.1 The derivation is highly informal and lacks proper mathematical definition/operations. Please provide a more neat derivation.
- 3.2 In these theoretical sections, instead of providing actual numbers for patch size, # of patches, # of nodes in the CP graph, etc. It is better to define them as variables. Then, authors could list those numbers in the experiments section or Appendix.
- 3.3 Do these weights recalculated in each training step, resulting in the reassignment of new core node patches?
- I think the brute search for finding out the optimal (CR, Accuracy) accuracy amongst 5*190 CP graph candidates is neither optimal nor efficient. In the future, if some researcher wants to adapt CP-ViT for some task, must he/she perform this kind of exhaustive search?
- Results on a larger and more prominent dataset such as ImageNet would increase the credibility of the method.
- Authors could compare the proposed method with other efficient ViT baselines that are mentioned in Related Works.
- 4.3 "...CP-ViT can effectively identity important meaningful patches.", I think identity=>identify. Should be corrected
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is overall well-written. Yet, there are some typos and ambiguities, which I pointed out in the Weaknesses section. If the authors could address those points, the overall clarity and quality of the paper increase. Technical novelty of the paper is pretty good. Authors provided the implementation details in the Appendix, which makes the results in this paper reproducible. Yet, authors could further provide an anonymous link to code for the project.
content.summary_of_the_review: A novel approach for redesigning ViT. I liked the paper, and after the proper revisions (by addressing/discussing the previously made points) I suggest acceptance to ICLR 23.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work proposes to apply Core-Periphery property from brain to the self-attention network, Vision Transformer (ViT), and thus propose a CP graph in ViT and build CP-ViT.  This work aims to borrow brain-inspired property and apply organizational principles of BNNs to ANN design and validation experiments are conducted on two image classification datasets
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The idea to apply some principles from the brain is interesting.
2. The visualization is clear and well demonstrates the advantages of the proposed method.

Weaknesses:
1. Core-Periphery principle is very similar to some token selection strategy, which is not new in ViT now as many works have adopted such stratages[1][2]. So the novelty of this work is somewhat weak. 
2. The improvement achieved by Core-Periphery graph is marginal compared with very naive ViT like Deit, and the proposed CP-ViT is only validated on very small datasets like CIFAR and INbreast. It would be better to validate on more datasets like ImageNet, and also apply the CO principle to more advance ViT such as Swin, T2T-ViT, PVT etc.



[1] Liang, Youwei, et al. "Not all patches are what you need: Expediting vision transformers via token reorganizations." ICLR 2022.
[2] Wang, Yulin, et al. "Not all images are worth 16x16 words: Dynamic vision transformers with adaptive sequence length." NeurIPS 2022
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The authors promise to release their codes for Reproducibility.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors of the paper propose to infuse the Core-Periphery principle commonly seen in BNNs (biological neural networks) into the design of vision transformer (ViT), which results in the so-called CP-ViT architecture. Specifically, the authors propose to upgrade the complete graph of dense connections in the original vanilla ViT with a sparse graph with Core-Periphery property (CP graph), where the core nodes are redesigned and reorganized to serve as a center for other periphery nodes to exchange information.
The authors empirically show that the optimal CP-ViT among all the investigated CP-ViTs can have better predictive performance than the original vanilla ViT with reduced computational costs; and the corresponding CP-ViT can significantly enhance the model interpretability since its core nodes can identify task-related meaningful and important image patches.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 
(1). The authors quantify the typical Core-Periphery (CP) organization of the human brain networks and infuse the corresponding CP principle into the design of vision transformer (ViT).  To my best knowledge, it is the first time that I see that the CP principle is used to construct the sparse connections in transformer, though I have already seen some other works of designing the sparse connections in transformer.  
(2). The experimental results show that the optimal CP-ViT among all the investigated CP-ViTs can have better predictive performance than the original vanilla ViT as well as the better model interpretability. Thus, the paper has shown some usefulness of the proposed CP-ViT.


Weaknesses:
(1). One big weakness is that the overall computation cost of finding the optimal CP-ViT among all the sampled (190 * 5) candidate CP-ViTs, which should be much larger than that of computing the single vanilla ViT. I suggest that the authors explicitly list the overall underlying computation cost of all the sampled (190 * 5) candidate CP-ViTs versus that of the original vanilla ViT.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The overall clarity of the paper is good so that I can understand the whole paper without difficulties. 

The quality of the paper is also OK. Please also see some questions and non-major issues that I list at the end.

There is some novelty since it is the first time that I see that the CP principle is used to construct the sparse connections in transformer. I also like Sec 4.3 which shows good model interpretability.


Questions and issues:

(1). For Equation (2) on page 4, V_j^{(r)} should be outside the activation function \sigma().  What is the definition of x_i^(r+1)?

(2). Similarly, for Equation (3) on page 5, V should be outside softmax function. 

(3). For Sec 3.3 on page 5, for the statement “we computed the gradients of the output y (before the activation function)”, could you define the output y? For Equation (4), should you add the absolute value sign around the gradient (since a gradient can be negative)?

(4). For Table 2 on page 8, are you sure that the performance advantage of the optimal CP-ViT over other ViTs does not come from randomness? Have you used multiple independent runs to ensure that the advantage is statistically significant?
content.summary_of_the_review:
The overall clarity and quality of the paper is not bad. There is some novelty in the paper since it is the first time that I see that the CP principle is used to construct the sparse connections in transformer. The model interpretability empirically shown in Sec 4.3 is what I like most. 

My main concern of the paper is the overall computation cost of all the sampled candidate CP-ViTs in order to find the optimal CP-ViT, though the computation cost of the optimal CP-ViT itself is smaller than that of the vanilla ViT. The paper does not provide an efficient method of finding the optimal CP-ViT.  Another place for future improvement is that using multiple independent runs to show that the performance advantage of the optimal CP-ViT over other ViTs (shown in Table 2) is statistically significant.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper aims to redesign the conventional dense self-attention mechanism with the brain-inspired sparse core-periphery (CP) graph to improve vision transformer’s performance (accuracy & computational cost) and interpretability. The proposed CP-ViT is enabled by three techniques including CP graph generation, CP-guided sparse self-attention and importance/gradient-based patch redistribution, and validated on two small datasets (INbreast & CIFAR-100).
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
+ (Clarity) The paper is mostly clearly written and easy to follow.

Weaknesses
- (Novelty) As opposed to what’s implied in the paper, applying neuroscience observations or principles to help create better deep learning models is quite far from a novel approach, as the topic has been extensively studied in the past [1], whether specifically using sparse interconnections [2] or not. Moreover, utilizing structured sparsity to accelerate attention also has been a common research theme in recent years [3, 4] where similar concepts such as blocks (nodes in this paper) [5], global (core) vs local (periphery) attention [6], sorting (patch redistribution) [7], etc. all have been studied. Without qualitative (Sec 2) and/or quantitative (Sec 4) comparisons against these prior work, the novelty of this paper is unfortunately rather unconvincing. Please expand Sec 2 & 4 to fairly include such comparisons.
- (Quality) The paper has two major issues in its quality.
1. The paper’s empirical validation is insufficient to support its claims (better accuracy & interpretability). Using only two small datasets (INbreast & CIFAR-100) for a purely empirical paper (no theoretical justification) isn’t really acceptable nowadays. Please consider including ImageNet (or at least Tiny ImageNet) results, as well as more baselines from [3-7]. In addition, please include standard deviations for all accuracy numbers in Table 2 to prove the statistical significance of CP-ViT’s improvement. Lastly, CP-ViT’s interpretability (Fig 5) should be directly compared against e.g. the attention maps of vanilla ViT (Fig 6, Dosovitskiy et al.) and other related baselines [3-7].
2. The claim about CP-ViT’s computational cost is very misleading, if not totally incorrect. There will be no saving at all if the attention is implemented as Eq (3). Even if a more sophisticated implementation as Eq (2) is used, the actual run time (e.g. on a GPU) is unlikely to see any improvement unless the connection ration (CR) is very low (e.g. <<50%), rendering most “sweet spots” in Table 2 likely not faster at all. Please include the actual run time numbers if the authors insist on making this claim.
- (Significance) Due to the aforementioned issues in the paper’s novelty and quality, it’s hard to conclude that this work is significant.

[1] Brain-inspired models for visual object recognition: an overview, Artificial Intelligence Review, January 2022.\
[2] A Brain-inspired Algorithm for Training Highly Sparse Neural Networks, https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.07138 \
[3] Efficient Transformers: A Survey, https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.06732 \
[4] A Practical Survey on Faster and Lighter Transformers, https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14636 \
[5] Blockwise Self-Attention for Long Document Understanding, EMNLP, 2020.\
[6] ETC: Encoding Long and Structured Inputs in Transformers, EMNLP, 2020.\
[7] Sparse Sinkhorn Transformer, ICML, 2020.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Please see above for my evaluation of the clarity, quality and novelty of the paper. All aspects of the paper (except for clarity) need to be substantially improved.

Regarding reproducibility, the submission didn’t include anonymized source code. However, given the overall simplicity of the paper, I believe it won’t be too hard to reproduce its results even without the source code.

Below are some additional questions for the authors.
* Is patch redistribution not performed during inference, since $y$ is not available for computing gradients? In this case, how does the network guarantee that semantically important patches are processed by the core nodes, given that the (spatial) distribution of such patches in the test set may not align with the training set at all?
* While the authors should more broadly compare their work against existing brain-inspired algorithms from e.g. [1-3], I also wonder how does CP-ViT compare against e.g. WS-ViT (as “small-worldness remains an important and viable concept in network neuroscience” [8]) and ER-ViT, since both graphs were already mentioned in the paper?

[8] Small-World Brain Networks Revisited, The Neuroscientist, 2017.
content.summary_of_the_review: In my opinion, since the paper is weak in nearly all aspects (novelty, quality and significance, except for clarity) and without sufficiently strong (e.g. SOTA) results, I unfortunately cannot recommend its acceptance to the conference.

content.title: CORE-PERIPHERY PRINCIPLE GUIDED REDESIGN OF SELF-ATTENTION IN TRANSFORMERS
content.abstract: Designing more efficient, reliable, and explainable neural network architectures is a crucial topic in the artificial intelligence (AI) field. Numerous efforts have been devoted to exploring the best structures, or structural signatures, of well-performing artificial neural networks (ANN). Previous studies, by post-hoc analysis, have found that the best-performing ANNs surprisingly resemble biological neural networks (BNN), which indicates that ANNs and BNNs may share some common principles to achieve optimal performance in either machine learning tasks or cognitive/behavior processes. Inspired by this phenomenon, rather than relying on post-hoc schemes, we proactively instill organizational principles of BNNs to guide the redesign of ANNs by infusing an efficient information communication mechanism of BNNs into ANNs. Specifically, we quantified the typical Core-Periphery (CP) organization of the human brain networks, infused the CorePeriphery principle into the redesign of the vision transformer (ViT), and proposed a novel CP-ViT architecture: the pair-wised densely interconnected self-attention architecture of ViT was upgraded by a sparse Core-Periphery architecture. In CPViT, the attention operation between nodes (image patches) is defined by a sparse graph with a Core-Periphery structure (CP graph), where the core nodes are redesigned and reorganized to play an integrative role and serve as a center for other periphery nodes to exchange information. We evaluated the proposed CP-ViT on multiple public datasets, including medical image datasets (INbreast) and natural image datasets (CIFAR-100). We show that there exist sweet spots of CP graphs that lead to CP-ViTs with significantly improved performance. In general, our work advances the state of the art in three aspects: 1) This work provides novel insights for brain-inspired AI: we can instill the efficient information communication mechanism of BNNs into ANNs by infusing similar organizational principles of BNNs into ANNs; 2) The optimized CP-ViT can significantly improve its predictive performance while dramatically reducing computational cost by benefiting from the infused efficient information communication mechanism existing in BNNs; and 3) The core nodes in CP-ViT can identify task-related meaningful and important image patches, which can significantly enhance the interpretability of the trained deep model. (Code is ready for release).
